essence: Directional Blur softens an image by averaging pixels along a single chosen axis, producing linear streaks rather than an all-direction blur. Direction sets the streak axis, Blur Length sets how far the sampling extends along that axis, and Effect Opacity mixes the blurred result back with the original.
manifests_as: Detail stretches and softens into straight, parallel streaks along the selected direction while detail perpendicular to that direction remains comparatively intact.

key_levers.name: Direction
key_levers.effect: Rotates the axis along which pixels are sampled and smeared; use it to align the blur with perceived motion, such as 0° for a horizontal-looking streak direction and 90° for a vertical-looking one.

key_levers.name: Blur Length
key_levers.effect: Increases the distance over which image detail is averaged along Direction; 0 produces no visible blur, while larger values create longer and softer streaks.

key_levers.name: Effect Opacity
key_levers.effect: Blends the processed directional blur with the unblurred source; lower values retain more original sharpness without changing the blur axis or length.

key_levers.name: GPU Rendering
key_levers.effect: Selects the effect's processing/rendering path; it is not intended as a creative blur-shape control, though implementation differences should be checked in the target render environment.

enums_to_verify.GPU Rendering (ADBE Force CPU GPU, 1-3): Unverified belief: these values choose among CPU/GPU or project-controlled rendering modes; verify the exact labels and whether any mode changes output consistency before relying on it.

reasoning_hooks: Blur Length defaults to 0, so changing Direction alone produces no visible result.
Direction defines an axis, not object motion detection: the effect blurs the entire processed layer uniformly along that line.
Animate Direction and/or Blur Length when the intended motion direction or intensity changes over time; a fixed value reads as a static smear.
Effect Opacity is a final mix control: reduce it to restore sharp source detail after choosing the actual streak direction and length.
This is not velocity-aware motion blur; moving objects, static backgrounds, and edge detail all receive the same directional sampling unless the effect is masked or isolated.
